name: Lucy MacLean, Positively Armed
oracle_text: Golden Rule — Whenever a token enters, you may have target player other than its controller create a token that's a copy of it, then you draw a card if an opponent created a token this way. Do this only once each turn.
blocked_sentences: Golden Rule — Whenever a token enters, you may have target player other than its controller create a token that's a copy of it, then you draw a card if an opponent created a token this way. Do this only once each turn.

needs.what: A `kind: "player"` target spec must be able to exclude a player named at trigger time -- "target player other than its controller", where "it" is the token the `token_created` event bound as `subject`. Two halves are missing: (a) `targeting._player_allowed` must honour the mapping forms of a player spec that `selectors.select_players` already parses (`controller_of`, `owner_of`, `binding`, `target`, `controller_of_target`) instead of only the three strings; and (b) there must be a *negated* player spec -- something like `{"not": {"controller_of": "subject"}}`, or a `not_controller` clause on the target selector -- because every existing mapping form names the players to allow and this line names the one player to forbid. Both `candidates` and `still_legal` route through `_player_allowed`, so fixing it there covers declaration and the 608.2b re-check.
needs.why_existing_wont_do: `targeting._player_allowed` is the whole of player-target legality and reads exactly one key: `clause = spec.selector.get("controller", "any")`, honouring only "you" (pid == controller) and "opponent" (pid != controller) and falling through to `return True` for anything else. Neither string is the printed restriction: the token's controller is whoever made the token, which on this card is routinely an opponent (it triggers on `controller: "any"`), so "opponent" wrongly forbids targeting yourself when an opponent's token enters and wrongly permits targeting the very opponent who made it, and "you"/"any" are further off still. Worse, the near miss loads *silently*: `selectors.validate_selector` accepts a Mapping `controller`, so `{"controller": {"controller_of": "subject"}}` compiles cleanly (verified against `compile_card`) and is then dropped on the floor by the `return True` fallthrough, yielding "target any player" -- a card that looks implemented and plays as a strictly wider one. And even if the mapping were honoured it is the inclusive set: `controller_of: "subject"` names the token's controller, which is precisely the player this line excludes, and `select_players` has no negation form at all. Splitting the ability in two (one trigger filtered `controller: "you"` targeting `controller: "opponent"`, one filtered `controller: "opponent"` targeting anyone) is not a workaround: it is still wrong in a pod, where "other than its controller" includes the other opponents, and `max_per_turn` is a per-ability cap, so two abilities would let "Do this only once each turn" happen twice.
needs.note: Nothing else on this card is blocked. `token_created` is a trigger event with the token bound as `subject`; `max_per_turn: 1` on the trigger is "Do this only once each turn"; `may` is "you may"; `copy_permanent` with `objects: {"binding": "subject"}` and `controller: {"target": "p"}` is "have target player create a token that's a copy of it"; and the conditional follow-up IS readable -- `copy_permanent` takes `as`, so `{"op": "if", "condition": {"exists": {"binding": "copies", "controller": "opponent"}}}` is exactly "if an opponent created a token this way". That whole ability minus the target restriction was confirmed to compile.
